title: Galakrond and the Five Proto-Dragons
summary: Galakrond's predation draws Tyr and five proto-dragons into a struggle that precedes the dragonflights' rise.
opening: Before the dragonflights had their charge, a hunger threatened the proto-dragons of ancient Azeroth. Tyr's answer depended on five who were not yet Aspects.

chapters.title: Galakrond's hunger
chapters.body: Galakrond’s hunger threatened the proto-dragons of ancient Azeroth. Those who lived beneath that danger could no longer ignore what he had become.

chapters.title: Tyr seeks allies
chapters.body: Tyr turned toward five proto-dragons. They had not yet received the charge of the Aspects, but the struggle would draw their lives together.

chapters.title: Five against one
chapters.body: Tyr and the five confronted Galakrond. The full measure of each part in that struggle remains to be recovered in this unfinished telling.

chapters.title: A charge for the future
chapters.body: After the danger passed, Tyr argued that the five should be empowered. Their victory became a beginning for the dragonflights’ greater duty.

reviewNote: The official overview is a strong lead; verify detailed motives, battle actions, and northern geography against the original story before promotion. Editorial chapter research tasks retained here: Establish what Galakrond became and why the other proto-dragons could not ignore him. Review the first-party history alongside the original story for the precise origin of his change. Trace Tyr's approach to the five proto-dragons and the different reasons they joined the fight. Their later titles should not be projected backward onto this moment. Follow the confrontation with Galakrond and identify each participant's contribution from primary narrative evidence before writing a finished battle sequence. Examine why Tyr argued for the five to be empowered after the danger passed, and where the story of the Aspects begins rather than ends.
